articles.title: Elena Furiase cuenta cómo Lolita descubrió que había perdido la virginidad: "Ya eres mujer"
articles.standfirst: La actriz madrileña y Marta Hazas han sido las invitadas de Pablo Motos este miércoles en 'El Hormiguero'
articles.summary: La actriz madrileña y Marta Hazas han sido las invitadas de Pablo Motos este miércoles en 'El Hormiguero'
articles.body: 'El Hormiguero' ha cerrado este miércoles la semana con la visita de las actrices Marta Hazas y Elena Furiase, quienes han presentado la película 'Hechos probados', que se estrenó en cines el 20 de noviembre. Se trata de un drama judicial que introduce, por primera vez en España, el género del 'true legal': una propuesta inspirada en casos reales y en la actividad de una 'legaltech', donde se traslada a la ficción conflictos jurídico-cotidianos. PABLO MOTOS. Presentáis 'Hechos probados', que ya está en los cines. Marta, ¿qué historia cuenta la película? MARTA HAZAS. Interpretamos a dos hermanas abogadas que atraviesan momentos vitales muy distintos. Mi personaje, Inés, es una mujer mucho más empática, muy centrada en cuidar a los demás, mientras que su hermana tiene un perfil más ambicioso y más orientado a los negocios. Trabajamos juntas en una legal tech, donde el personaje de Elena es mi jefa. A partir de ahí se desarrollan varios casos basados en hechos reales que vamos resolviendo a lo largo de la película. Mi hermana la interpreta Amaia Salamanca y el conflicto entre ambas tiene mucho peso en la historia. PABLO MOTOS. En la película, el conflicto entre hermanas es importante. Elena, ¿es verdad que tú y tu hermano Guillermo siempre os habéis cubierto las espaldas cuando alguno hacía alguna trastada? ELENA FURIASE. Sí, eso es totalmente cierto. Cuando éramos más jóvenes, nos protegíamos muchísimo. Ahora ya somos mayores y no hacemos tantas locuras, pero cuando pasaba algo, siempre nos ayudábamos. Si uno necesitaba que el otro le sacara de algún apuro, allí estábamos. Lo curioso es que mi madre siempre terminaba enterándose de todo. PABLO MOTOS. ¿Y cómo os descubría Lolita? ELENA FURIASE. Porque tiene una intuición increíble. Siempre digo que mi madre fue el ChatGPT antes de que existiera ChatGPT. Le hacías una pregunta y ya sabía la respuesta antes incluso de que ocurrieran las cosas. Tenía una capacidad asombrosa para leer las situaciones. PABLO MOTOS. De hecho, has contado alguna vez que supo que habías perdido la virginidad sin que le dijeras nada. ELENA FURIASE. Sí, fue exactamente así. Llegué a casa por la mañana después de una noche muy especial y, cuando entré, me pidió que fuera a hablar con ella. Me senté y, sin rodeos, me dijo: "Ya eres mujer". Yo me puse a llorar inmediatamente. Había acertado por completo. Fue un momento muy bonito y muy emocionante. PABLO MOTOS. Elena, en la película aparecen personajes bastante oportunistas. ¿Es cierto que cuando empezabas en esta profesión pensabas que todo el mundo era bueno y terminabas contando tu vida a cualquiera? ELENA FURIASE. Sí, absolutamente. Sigo pensando que la mayoría de la gente es buena, aunque los malos hagan mucho ruido. Cuando empecé, cualquier compañero amable me parecía automáticamente un amigo. Esta profesión puede ser bastante solitaria y yo siempre buscaba refugio en la gente que tenía cerca. Con el tiempo entendí que una persona puede ser encantadora contigo sin que necesariamente forme parte de tu círculo íntimo. No es que haya gente mala, simplemente no todo el mundo tiene el mismo interés o el mismo vínculo contigo. MARTA HAZAS. Yo recuerdo perfectamente conocer a Elena durante El Internado. Estábamos en el Festival de Málaga y me llamó muchísimo la atención su manera de ver el mundo. Me transmitía una enorme nobleza. Pensé que tenía un corazón inmenso y una confianza muy bonita en la gente. PABLO MOTOS. Marta, en una profesión donde hay mucho ego, ¿qué has aprendido de la gente falsa? MARTA HAZAS. He aprendido a ir con orejeras y centrarme en lo mío. No me interesa demasiado perder energía en eso. Sí he vivido situaciones en las que una persona te trata fenomenal en un determinado contexto y, de repente, en otro donde ya no resultas tan interesante, parece que ni te conoce. Al principio duele un poco, pero después entiendes que dice más de la otra persona que de ti. ELENA FURIASE. Y además Marta es exactamente igual siempre. Si te trata con cariño la primera vez, la segunda te trata aún mejor y la tercera mejor todavía. Hemos pasado mucho tiempo sin vernos y cada vez que nos reencontramos siempre ha sido igual de cariñosa conmigo. PABLO MOTOS. Hablando de rarezas, Marta, ¿es cierto que tienes fobia a las estatuas? MARTA HAZAS. Sí, y es una cosa bastante absurda porque ni siquiera la entiendo. Tiene nombre, se llama automatonofobia, pero en mi caso no son los muñecos lo que me da miedo. Me asustan las estatuas gigantes, las esculturas colosales, todo aquello que resulta desmesurado. PABLO MOTOS. ¿Qué sientes exactamente cuando estás delante de una? MARTA HAZAS. Una sensación muy extraña, como si pudiera cobrar vida. Sé que es irracional y me repito constantemente que no va a ocurrir nada, pero hay algo que me paraliza. Me pasa con esculturas enormes, con bustos y hasta con determinadas figuras que aparecen por sorpresa. Lo peor es el factor sorpresa. Entrar en una iglesia, girar una esquina y encontrarme una escultura delante me produce muchísimo rechazo. PABLO MOTOS. ¿La Estatua de la Libertad, por ejemplo? MARTA HAZAS. Horrible. No podría estar cerca. El David de Miguel Ángel también me daría mucho respeto, aunque sea una obra maravillosa. Me gusta el arte y disfruto visitando museos, pero determinadas esculturas me generan una sensación física muy difícil de explicar. PABLO MOTOS. Elena, tú tienes una fobia diferente: las lesiones y las roturas de huesos ELENA FURIASE. Sí, no tanto los huesos en sí como todo lo relacionado con fracturas, luxaciones y lesiones de ese tipo. Si alguien empieza a contarme que se desencajó una rodilla o un hombro, me pongo fatal. Lo pasó realmente mal. PABLO MOTOS. Tanto que durante una mudanza preferiste no acercarte a ayudar a tu pareja cuando se lesionó una rodilla. ELENA FURIASE. Totalmente cierto. Estaba embarazada de mi segunda hija y estábamos haciendo una mudanza. De repente oí un golpe enorme y a mi marido gritar que se había hecho daño en la rodilla. Yo empecé a imaginarme la rótula fuera de sitio y todo tipo de escenarios espantosos. No fui capaz de acercarme porque sabía que me iba a marear. Le pregunté si quería que llamara a su madre o a su hermano, pero no podía enfrentarme a la posibilidad de ver algo relacionado con la lesión. PABLO MOTOS. Marta, también tenéis una costumbre curiosa en casa. Cuando recibís una mala noticia profesional, abrís una botella de champán. MARTA HAZAS. Sí, empezó hace años, cuando estábamos intentando sacar adelante proyectos audiovisuales y recibíamos negativas continuamente. Había épocas en las que todo eran puertas cerradas. Un día teníamos una botella de champán en casa y decidimos abrirla precisamente después de recibir otro "no". Lo hicimos un poco por rebeldía. PABLO MOTOS. ¿Y funcionó? MARTA HAZAS. Nos ayudó a cambiar la perspectiva. Pensamos que cada negativa nos acercaba a algo diferente y probablemente mejor. Desde entonces, cuando aparece una mala noticia, intentamos celebrarla de alguna manera porque significa que toca buscar una nueva oportunidad. PABLO MOTOS. Elena, cambiando de tema, también eres una apasionada de las vajillas. ELENA FURIASE. Sí, lo reconozco abiertamente. Me encantan. Soy una auténtica enamorada de las vajillas bonitas. PABLO MOTOS. ¿Cuántas tienes? ELENA FURIASE. Me gusta encontrar diseños bonitos. No tienen por qué ser carísimas. Puedes encontrar vajillas preciosas en muchos sitios. De hecho, cuando me preguntan qué quiero para Reyes o para mi cumpleaños, muchas veces respondo que una vajilla nueva. Siempre me hace ilusión. PABLO MOTOS. Marta, además de la película, sigues de gira con Un matrimonio sin filtros. MARTA HAZAS. Sí, seguimos con la gira. Cerraremos esta etapa en Santander durante diciembre, pero el próximo año regresaremos a Madrid. Estaremos en el Teatro Alcázar a partir del 11 de febrero, que además coincide con el cumpleaños de Javi, así que tendremos doble motivo para celebrarlo. PABLO MOTOS. Para terminar, ¿qué os gustaría que encontrara el espectador en 'Hechos probados'? MARTA HAZAS. Una historia entretenida, cercana y con personajes muy humanos. ELENA FURIASE. Y también una reflexión sobre la familia, sobre los vínculos y sobre cómo afrontamos los problemas desde puntos de vista muy distintos. Creo que el público puede sentirse muy identificado con las dos hermanas.

articles.summary: Paradas do Dia de Ação de Graças nos EUA celebram 100 anos com desfiles históricos, balões gigantes e shows de Lizzo e Queen Latifah em Nova York e outras cidades.
articles.body:

O tradicional desfile de infláveis gigantes da rede de lojas de departamento Macy's, que arrasta multidões para as ruas de Nova York anualmente, foi adiado para sábado (28) por conta da previsão de chuva forte para a cidade norte-americana.

O desfile é o principal de uma série de paradas pelo Dia de Ação de Graças nos Estados Unidos que, neste ano, completam cem anos de existência .

A parada de "Thanksgiving" da Macy’s, que originalmente ocorreria nesta quinta-feira (26), também vai festejar seu centenário com novidades.

Em Nova Orleans, a Natchitoches Christmas Festival, considerada uma das celebrações natalinas mais antigas do país, também chega à marca, assim como a America’s Thanksgiving Parade, em Detroit.

O desfile mais antigo de Dia de Ação de Graças dos EUA ocorre na Filadélfia. A 6abc Dunkin’ Thanksgiving Day Parade realizará sua 107ª edição em 2026.

Conheça, abaixo, algumas das paradas mais famosas e saiba quando elas irão acontecer:

O 100º desfile anual do Dia de Ação de Graças da Macy's vai agora no sábado, dia 28 de novembro, em Nova York, das 8h30 às 12h (pelo horário local), e será transmitido ao vivo pela emissora americana NBC.

Vários artistas como Queen Latifah, Teddy Swims e Natasha Bedingfield irão se apresentar no evento, que contará com 100 bonecos infláveis - entre eles, novidades como o Mickey Aprendiz de Feiticeiro e a Hello Kitty.

A parada foi adiada pela primeira vez em cem anos por conta da previsão de chuva fote em Nova York nesta quinta.

"A segurança de nossos participantes e espectadores é nossa prioridade máxima e, após uma consulta minuciosa com nossos parceiros na cidade e em órgãos públicos, tomamos a decisão de alterar a realização da celebração deste ano", informou a Macy's em um comunicado divulgado na quarta-feira (25).

Balão do Olaf, de Frozen, em desfile de Ação de Graças da Macy's — Foto: Eduardo Munoz Alvarez/AP

A festa de Ação de Graças de Nova Orleans, na Lousiana, durará três dias, todo fim de semana de feriado, entre 27 e 29 de novembro.

Os festejos fazem parte de um evento maior, que começou no sábado (21) e vai até o dia 6 de janeiro, com vários programas para famílias comemorarem as festas de fim de ano.

A primeira delas, o Thanksgiving, terá a tradicional iluminação ao longo do Cane River Lake, com mais de 300 mil luzes e 100 instalações decorativas, todas as noites ao entardecer.

Realizada em Detroit, o desfile de Ação de Graças que percorre aproximadamente 4,8 km pela histórica Woodward Avenue irá acontecer no dia 26, a partir das 8h45.

Bandas marciais e celebridades locais como a Miss Michigan e ex-atletas do estado irão desfilar junto com 33 carros alegóricos e cinco balões gigantes.

articles.title: Leo Tomassini convida à escuta de valsa com Guinga enquanto aguarda a edição do álbum 'Jaula de gorila' em 2027 | G1
articles.body:
Leo Tomassini lança em 1º de dezembro o single 'Claro da lua', gravado com Guinga — Foto: Fernanda Vogas / Divulgação

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

♬ “Escuta comigo o claro da lua / Valsa comigo a valsa do nada / Me dê a mão, me dê a mão / Vamos flutuar no azul”, convida Guinga, com a voz grave, profunda e quase etérea, nos versos iniciais de “Claro da lua”, single que Leo Tomassini lançará em 1º de dezembro.

Tomassini também canta a valsa lírica que compôs por volta de 2007 ou 2008, mas, devoto de Guinga, preferia nem ter posto voz na música gravada com produção musical e o toque do violão de Jean Charnaux.

“Minha ideia inicial e sonho era ter a voz de Guinga do início ao fim. Queria ter minha obra cantada por essa voz mágica. Não há cantor ou cantora no mundo melhor que Guinga. Há tão bons quanto, Chet Baker, João Gilberto, Billie Holiday, Ella Fitzgerald, Gal... Lamento estar ao lado dele nessa faixa. Sinto-me uma cantora dessas muitas que por aí vão atravancando nosso caminho, cheias de assepsias técnicas e zero calor e vida. Tudo na voz de Guinga ganha uma densidade e intenção naturais, o que se canta é vivido”, caracteriza um embevecido Leo Tomassini, cantor e compositor carioca revelado como vocalista da Família Roitman, banda carioca que esteve cena de 1989 a 2003 com nome inspirado no clã disfuncional da novela “Vale tudo” (1988).

Em carreira solo desde 2003, ano em que lançou o álbum “Amor e cordas”, Leo Tomassini aguarda a edição do terceiro álbum solo em 2027, “Jaula de gorila”, gravado sob direção musical do guitarrista Pedro Sá.

Inteiramente autoral, o repertório do álbum “Jaula de gorila” é composto pelas músicas “45 km” (Leo Tomassini e Chacal), “Álcool gel” (Leo Tomassini), “Baião das estrelas” (Leo Tomassini e Mauro Aguiar), “Fim” (Leo Tomassini e Beto Valente), “Gravidade” (Leo Tomassini), “Luz versus luz” (Leo Tomassini a partir de versos de Paulo Leminski), “Pop Cacaso Pop” (Leo Tomassini a partir de versos de Cacaso), “Rápido e rasteiro” (Leo Tomassini e Chacal), “Rapunzel” (Leo Tomassini), “Rei do vermelho e o negro” (Leo Tomassini e Joaquim Tomassini), “Sobre a existência de Deus” (Leo Tomassini) e “Uma voz” (Leo Tomassini a partir de versos de Ferreira Gullar), além da música-título “Jaula de gorila” (Leo Tomassini e Cabelo).

Valsa que Tomassini assina com Jean Charnaux e com o filho Joaquim Tomassini, ambos creditados como autores da composiçãporque cada um sugeriu a mudança de uma nota da melodia, “Claro da lua” não faz parte do repertório do álbum “Jaula de gorila”.

No entanto, a devoção a Guinga conecta o vindouro single avulso viabilizado pela Vogas Produções com o ainda inédito álbum gravado com produção orquestrada por Leo Tomassini com Beno Ibeas e Pedro Sá. A música que encerra o álbum, “Fim”, tem letra arrematada com o verso “Escrevi no chão com tinta: eu te amo, Guinga”.

articles.title: Festival de Frutos do Mar movimenta Rio das Ostras de 26 a 29 de novembro | G1

articles.body:
Música ao vivo e gastronomia são um casamento perfeito para quem procura um final de semana diferente — Foto: Secom

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Quatro dias de gastronomia e música brasileira vão movimentar a região da Boca da Barra, em Rio das Ostras. De 26 a 29 de novembro, a Praia do Cemitério recebe a 27ª edição do Festival de Frutos do Mar, que neste ano tem como tema “Maré Musical Brasileira”. O evento reúne 16 participações de estabelecimentos locais, com receitas inspiradas em artistas, álbuns e canções nacionais, além de apresentações musicais gratuitas.

“O Festival será um grande sucesso porque é tradição na cidade. Contem com o apoio da Administração Municipal porque sabemos que comida é mais que alimento. É cultura e preservação da memória. Esse é um evento do Calendário Oficial que já em sua 27ª Edição. Isso mostra que é um evento consolidado e que mostra a qualidade dos Restaurantes. Justifica também o crescimento da Gastronomia no Município”, disse Rosemarie Teixeira, presidente da Fundação Rio das Ostras de Cultura, que representou o prefeito Carlos Augusto Balthazar.

O Festival de Frutos do Mar será realizado na Praia do Cemitério, na região da Boca da Barra, no Centro de Rio das Ostras. A combinação de gastronomia, música e programação à beira-mar oferece ao público uma oportunidade de conhecer a produção dos estabelecimentos locais e aproveitar atrações culturais durante o fim de semana.

A entrada no festival é gratuita. As entradas gastronômicas custam R$ 28 e os pratos principais, R$ 40. Bebidas e sobremesas terão preços próprios. Na quinta e na sexta-feira, dias 26 e 27, o funcionamento será das 17h à meia-noite. No sábado e no domingo, dias 28 e 29, o público poderá visitar o espaço a partir do meio-dia, também até a meia-noite.

A programação musical começa na quinta, dia 26, às 18h, com Micha e Rodolpho Mendes, seguida pelo show da banda KM 50, às 20h. Na sexta-feira, dia 27, Rafael Spitz se apresenta às 18h e Omnia Vincit, às 20h. No sábado, dia 28, as atrações são Baleias Voadoras, às 15h; cortejo com Ostras Band, às 17h; As Florroseiras, às 18h; e Luan Schuenckel, às 20h. No domingo, dia 29, o Segundo Set Instrumental abre a programação às 14h, seguido por Maycon Melo, às 17h, e Cláudia Falcão, às 19h, que encerra o festival.

“A proposta desta edição é aproximar a culinária da música brasileira. Cada estabelecimento participante criou receitas com nomes ou referências a artistas e obras musicais. O festival não terá competição gastronômica. A iniciativa tem como foco a valorização da gastronomia local e dos sabores do mar”, explicou Jamile Freitas, presidente do Núcleo Gourmet.

O evento é realizado pelo Núcleo Gourmet, em parceria com a Fundação Rio das Ostras de Cultura, e conta com o apoio institucional da Prefeitura de Rio das Ostras e Câmara de Vereadores, além do apoio do Sesc, do Sindicomércio, do Serviço Autônomo de Água e Esgoto - SAAE e da Rio+.

articles.title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster
articles.summary: US company Fender is in dispute with a German firm that makes generic versions of its key model.
articles.body:
Hans Thomann leads the way through his music store in central Germany to the large electric guitar department, where the walls are hung with hundreds of instruments.

Brands on show include famous names Fender and Gibson, plus Harley Benton.

The latter is a low-price range of guitars owned by the family-run company that Thomann leads – Thomann, one of the world's largest online retailers of musical instruments.

The shop, together with warehouses and offices, are at the company's headquarters in the tiny village of Treppendorf in rural Upper Franconia, in Bavaria.

The business was founded by Thomann's father, Hans Thomann Senior, in 1954.

In one corner of the store, a young man is trying out a Fender Stratocaster, one of the world's most iconic electric guitars.

Designed in the US in the early 1950's, the "Strat" became the instrument of choice for many famous rock and pop musicians, such as Jimi Hendrix, Eric Clapton and Buddy Holly.

Hendrix famously set one on fire at the Monterey Pop Festival in 1967, and his performances helped make the guitar a symbol of modern rock music.

These days, the Stratocaster is very much on Hans Thomann's mind, because it's the subject of an intense copyright dispute.

When the guitar was first made, California-based Fender did not trademark the body shape. So, since the 1960s Strat-shaped guitars have been made and sold around the world by countless manufacturers.

The shape is so ubiquitous that many musicians consider it to be a generic design.

But since March of this year, Fender has begun a new campaign to defend its right to the guitar's sinuous shape. It follows a decision by a court in Düsseldorf last December which granted Fender copyright protection of the Stratocaster design in Germany.

The defendant, Chinese seller Yiwu Philharmonic Musical Instruments, did not appear. The Düsseldorf court accepted Fender's arguments and ruled in its favour. According to German law the court makes its decision based on the facts presented by the plaintiff if the defendant doesn't raise objections.

The ruling said that Fender's design for the Stratocaster was "an outstanding, free creative achievement" that "clearly reflects the personality of its author".

It described the guitar as "a body without edges" with "soft curves that evoke associations with the female torso consisting of hips, waist and arms".

On its website, Fender announced in March the decision created "enforceable rights" against any guitars using the Strat body shape, that are manufactured, sold or distributed into Germany or other EU countries, "regardless of where those guitars are produced".

Fender began to send out cease and desist letters to dozens of retailers and manufacturers, both large and small, asking them to stop making and selling Strat lookalikes heading for Europe.

One of these letters, seen by the BBC, said Fender "insists that you immediately stop manufacturing, marketing, selling and producing the infringing products".

The letter also demanded that companies recall and destroy the guitars.

The move caused an outcry in the guitar world, among manufacturers and musicians.

"Time to boycott Fender," one person wrote on the Facebook page of the boutique US guitar maker, LSL Instruments.

Thomann received a cease-and-desist letter shortly after a visit to Treppendorf in March by Fender's chief executive Bud Cole.

"We remember the meeting as a very positive and constructive exchange," says Thomann. "At the time we had no indication that Fender was considering legal action."

"For more than 70 years, we have carried Fender instruments with great appreciation for the brand and many of us are Fender players ourselves. We were therefore surprised and disappointed by Fender's recent actions."

In 2025, Thomann sold over 112,000 Strat-style guitars, including more than 16,000 made by Fender and Fender subsidiary brand Squier.

"As a retailer, we want to continue offering our customers everything that is available in the world of guitars," adds Thomann. "We would have welcomed to the opportunity to discuss the matter openly before receiving a formal legal demand for such extreme action."

In June, Thomann the company started legal action against Fender, filing an "action of non-infringement" that said that Fender does not have a valid copyright claim to the Stat shape.

Thomann says that the Düsseldorf ruling was simply a default judgement based on missed deadlines and didn't represent a "comprehensive review of the legal claims".

For its part, Fender, which is majority-owned by Hawaii-based company Servco Pacific, says it has a responsibility to protect the Stratocaster's iconic design. In July, it sued Thomann in a German court, for copyright infringement.

In a statement to the BBC, Fender said it remained "confident" in the original Düsseldorf court judgement.

"Our preference has always been to keep lines of communication open and resolve these matters through constructive dialogue rather than litigation," it added.

With the legal cases continuing, Thomann says he believes it is important to get "legal clarity – not only for us but for the wider guitar industry."

"Ultimately, we want to help preserve an environment in which innovation, diversity and creative development can continue to thrive," he adds.

Thomann says he was taking legal action not just for his company, but for smaller music companies too.

"We used to be a small music shop ourselves," he says.

"Many of the smaller manufacturers, guitar makers and dealers affected simply don't have the financial and legal resources to conduct a legal dispute like this."

One such company is LSL Instruments, a family-owned boutique guitar maker in California. Its director of sales, Johny Miller, told me that when they first received Fender's letter they were "pretty terrified and blown away".

"They were asking us to retrieve guitars from dealers out there and destroy them and send them proof.

"So when we heard Hans Thomann got the same letter and responded by suing them… so that everybody in the guitar community could understand exactly what's going on… we were so thankful and grateful," he says.

Fender tells BBC that it agrees that "legal clarity was important", and that it was now focusing more on targeting larger manufacturers.

It also says it realises that "our outreach has caused concern and frustration, particularly among smaller, independent guitar builders. "To them we say: we continue to hear you, and we're listening."

articles.body: Bollywood superstar Shah Rukh Khan has reportedly sent a legal notice to social media influencer over an alleged 'defamatory' Instagram reel.Suvigya Sharma, an influencer, reportedly found himself in a legal soup over allegations that he made a 'mischievous, misleading and defamatory' claim about the actor's recent appearance at spiritual leader Sadhguru's event.The viral reel featured footage of SRK in conversation with other guests. However, Sharma, in his post, claimed that Shah Rukh was asked to "remain silent" during the interaction, as reported by India Today. In a legal notice dated November 23, Khan's legal representatives alleged that the caption accompanying the video was intended to distort the context of the interaction and damage the actor's image and reputation.As per the report, the notice, citing Section 356, stated that the allegations were entirely baseless and false, adding that circulating such content without evidence could adversely affect the actor's public image.Citing Section 356 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, which deals with defamation, the legal notice stated that individuals cannot circulate false and damaging statements about public figures without substantiated evidence.Sharma has reportedly been given 48 hours to comply with five demands and provide written confirmation of the actions taken. These include immediately removing the Instagram reel, refraining from sharing or circulating the claim further, and deleting or correcting the captions and statements associated with the video.The notice has also directed the influencer to preserve the original footage and all records related to the publication of the content. Sharma has been asked to provide written confirmation within 48 hours that all the demands have been complied with.On the work front, SRK is currently gearing up for the release of his ambitious action film 'King' that is slated for a Christmas release. articles.title: Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt settle winery fight lawsuit that surfaced abuse allegations
articles.summary: The long-running legal battles between Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt have come to an end a decade after the A-list celebrity couple split, with the actors settling a dispute over the ownership of a French winery.
articles.body: The long-running legal battles between Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt have come to an end a decade after the A-list celebrity couple split, with the actors settling a dispute over the ownership of a French winery. The actors said in a joint statement Wednesday that they had reached a settlement of the lawsuit, which transcended business matters when a legal filing from Jolie surfaced abuse allegations against Pitt. “We have settled out of court in the best interests of our family and will not be commenting further,” the statement provided by representatives for Pitt, 62, and Jolie, 51, said. Jolie filed for divorce in 2016, citing the “health of the family,” after a private jet flight from Europe. The couple’s use of private judges — an increasingly common move among splitting celebrities in recent years — kept the details of the divorce largely under wraps, even after it was settled at the very end of 2024. But the winery lawsuit became a way for details of their dispute to become public. Pitt sued Jolie in 2022, saying she had abandoned an agreement that he would buy her half of Chateau Miraval, a French winery they owned together. She instead sold her part to the Tenute del Mondo wine group. Pitt said it was a “vindictive” and “unlawful” move that should not have been made without his consent and ruined a private space that had been a second home. The descriptions of the abuse alleged on the private flight weren’t public until Jolie filed a cross-complaint in the dispute. Jolie and her attorneys said Pitt had demanded she sign a wide-ranging nondisclosure agreement about him as part of the proposed deal that was an attempt to cover up his abuse of her and the children. The FBI and child services officials had investigated Pitt’s actions on the flight, centering on the treatment of their eldest son. The FBI released a statement in late 2016 saying it would not investigate further, and the U.S. attorney did not bring charges. Pitt has denied being abusive but did not defend his behavior on the flight. Pitt said in a 2017 interview with GQ that he had a drinking problem at the time, but had since become sober and was going to therapy. In an interview with Esquire earlier this year, he said he was sober for seven years but had started drinking again “in a more restrained manner.” A heavily redacted FBI report obtained by The Associated Press in 2022 said an agent provided a probable cause statement to prosecutors on Pitt, but that after discussing the merits, “it was agreed by all parties that criminal charges would not be pursued.” The document said Jolie was “personally conflicted” about supporting charges, and in a later court filing she said she opted not to push for them for the sake of the family. All six children are now adults; the youngest — twins Knox and Vivienne — turned 18 in July. Many of the Jolie-Pitt children have reportedly since dropped their father’s surname. Publicly, both Pitt and Jolie have been extremely tight-lipped on everything surrounding their split, despite robust promotional tours for various projects — including the Pitt-starrer “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth,” which also landed in select theaters Wednesday. Both were among the most elite stars in film when they began dating in 2004, after co-starring as hitman-and-hitwoman spouses in “Mr. & Mrs. Smith.” The star of “Maleficent” and “Lara Croft: Tomb Raider,” Jolie won an Oscar for her performance in 1999’s “Girl, Interrupted.” Pitt, the star of “Fight Club” and “Inglourious Basterds,” thrived as both actor and producer after the split. He won his own Academy Award for 2019’s “Once Upon a Time ... in Hollywood,” the crowning achievement in an awards season that some in media framed as a redemption and brought major public affection for him. Jolie kept a less visible profile in the years since the divorce, though she directed several films and appeared in several more while trying to focus on raising the children. She was nominated for an Oscar for her portrayal of the legendary soprano Maria Callas in “Maria” and starred in “Couture,” released this summer.

articles.title: Director Sampath Nandi explains violence in Sharwanand’s ‘Bhogi’; says, ‘It is not forced violence, it comes naturally from the story’
articles.summary: Director Sampath Nandi has spoken about the violence in his upcoming film ‘Bhogi’, starring Sharwanand.
articles.body: Director Sampath Nandi has spoken about the violence in his upcoming film ‘Bhogi’, starring Sharwanand. The filmmaker said that the violent scenes are an important part of the story and have not been added just to create an impact. He also spoke about the film being sent to the Central Board of Film Certification's (CBFC) Revising Committee and how the decision affected the film's promotions. ‘Bhogi’ is now scheduled to release in theatres on November 27.Sampath Nandi talks about violence in ‘Bhogi’In an interview with The New Indian Express, Sampath Nandi explained why the film has violent scenes. He said, “It is not forced violence; it comes naturally from the story.”The director also said that the team did not expect the film to be sent to the Revising Committee. He admitted that the decision affected their promotional plans.“We never wanted the film to go to the revising committee, but that was the CBFC's suggestion. I agree that we did not have enough time for promotions, but I believe in my content,” he said.‘Bhogi’ release postponed after CBFC issue‘Bhogi’ was initially scheduled to release on November 13. The makers had planned a trailer launch and a pre-release event. However, the CBFC sent the film to its Revising Committee instead of giving it a clearance certificate. Following this, the makers postponed the release and stopped their promotional activities. The film will now arrive in theatres on November 27.‘Bhogi’ inspired by a real-life incidentSampath Nandi also shared how he got the idea for ‘Bhogi’. During his childhood, he came across a man who performed superstitious rituals and travelled through villages near his hometown. Years later, he read a newspaper report about a similar incident near the Adilabad-Maharashtra border.“When I was a child, there was a village called Ramagiri Gutta, around 50 kilometres from our village. As I grew older, I came across a newspaper clipping about a similar incident that had happened near the Adilabad-Maharashtra border. articles.title: U2 Perform Dolly Parton’s Final Recording During NFL Halftime Show
articles.summary: The band delivered the moving Parton and Bono duet, "Torn," during Wednesday night's performance
articles.body:
On the eve of Thanksgiving at the NFL halftime show, U2 performed the Dolly Parton and Bono duet, " Torn ," as the country great's image was projected on screens surrounding the stage.

It was a poignant moment during the show, as the song was the final vocal recording of Parton's seven-decade career. The track appears on U2's recently debuted album, Carnaval de Luz . While Parton, who shares writing credits for the song with the band and Snow Patrol's Johnny McDaid, originally wrote "Torn" around a story of a woman trying to choose between two men, Bono and McDaid rewrote the lyrics around a mother watching her family divided. "You name the location," Bono told Rolling Stone for U2's recent cover story , "but everyone knows what it is.… People say in the U.S. now, people are scared to go into Thanksgiving."

Parton, who died in August at age 80, recorded her part on the album's closing track in June. "When she got ill," Bono said, "she got out of her bed to sing this song. And you can hear that. And I can't even listen to it now."

U2's halftime show during the NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve game between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams aired on Netflix . The streamer has been organizing special halftime performances since it began airing select NFL games a few years ago. Beyoncé performed at Netflix's first NFL game on Christmas Day 2024, while Snoop Dogg took the stage last year.

During U2's performance on during Wednesday's show at Sofi Stadium, the band was joined by a massive marching choir and the Womack Sisters, who were recently nominated for Best New Artist and Best Traditional R&B Performance ("If I Let You") at the 69th Grammys.

articles.title: King Crimson co-founder Michael Giles passes away at 84; look back at the legendary drummer's musical journey
articles.summary: Michael Giles, the drummer and vocalist who co-founded the progressive rock band King Crimson, has passed away at the age of 84.
articles.body: Michael Giles, the drummer and vocalist who co-founded the progressive rock band King Crimson, has passed away at the age of 84. The musician died on Monday, according to the band's record label, DGM. The label confirmed the news but did not share the cause of death. His passing has prompted tributes from fans who remember his contribution to the evolution of progressive rock.DGM issued a statement acknowledging Giles' influence on musicians across generations. The label highlighted his creative approach and lasting impact on the genre. According to PEOPLE, Michael Giles is survived by his sister Marion, brother Peter, five children — Tina, Amanda, William, Rosie and Oliver — and his grandchildren.DGM remembers Michael Giles' contribution to progressive rockThe record label paid tribute to the musician following his death. Its statement recognized his originality, musical curiosity and commitment to artistic freedom. DGM said, "Michael's originality, musical curiosity and uncompromising commitment to creative freedom challenged conventions and inspired generations of musicians around the world. He leaves behind an extraordinary musical legacy, and his unique contribution to the evolution of progressive music will never be forgotten."Michael Giles became an important part of the progressive rock movement through his work with King Crimson. His distinctive drumming helped shape the band's early sound and its influence on the genre.From Giles, Giles and Fripp to King CrimsonBorn in Bournemouth, England, in 1942, Michael Giles began his musical career alongside his brother Peter Giles. In 1967, the brothers joined guitarist Robert Fripp to form Giles, Giles and Fripp. The group released its only studio album in 1968.The following year, Michael Giles and Robert Fripp formed King Crimson with Greg Lake, Ian McDonald and Peter Sinfield. The band's debut album, 'In the Court of the Crimson King', was released in 1969. It went on to become one of progressive rock's defining records and helped establish the group as a major force in the genre.Michael Giles continued working with former bandmatesMichael Giles, Ian McDonald and Greg Lake left King Crimson in 1970. However, Michael Giles and Greg Lake contributed to the band's second album, 'In the Wake of Poseidon'. That year, Michael Giles also collaborated with Ian McDonald on an album released under their names.His musical associations with former collaborators continued over the following decades. In 2002, he reunited with Peter Giles, Greg Lake and Ian McDonald to form the 21st Century Schizoid Band. Guitarist Jakko Jakszyk was also part of the lineup. The group took its name from King Crimson's popular track '21st Century Schizoid Man'.Fans pay tribute to the legendary drummerFollowing the announcement, fans took to X to remember Michael Giles and celebrate his contribution to music. One user wrote, "Rest in peace legend ." Another shared, "I was a teen and I wanted to look like him and have a girlfriend like her. RIP legend."A fan highlighted his influence on drumming, writing, "One of the most influential drummers of all times, the most important prog rock drummer beside Bill Bruford." Another tribute read, "Sad news …king Crimson were a truly innovative and amazing prog band and great live."Remembering his work on the band's iconic song, another fan wrote, "the legend that give us that amazing drumming in "21st Century Schizoid Man", rest in peace michael ."Solo projects and later musical releasesBeyond his work with King Crimson and its former members, Michael Giles explored independent projects. He recorded his solo album 'Progress' in 1983, although it was not released until 2002. He subsequently formed the Michael Giles MAD BAND, which released albums in 2009 and 2011.Earlier this year, the musician added another release to his discography with the compilation album 'Shadows/Solo'. His career spanned several decades, with projects that reflected his continued interest in exploring different musical ideas.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Judge temporarily blocks FCC from reviewing ABC station licenses amid First Amendment fight
articles.summary: A federal judge blocked the FCC from an early review of ABC's broadcast licenses, citing a likely First Amendment victory and a campaign of retaliation.
articles.body: A federal judge on Wednesday blocked the Federal Communications Commission from conducting an early review of ABC's broadcast station licenses, siding with The Walt Disney Company-owned media network's position that the Trump administration's move would have a chilling effect on First Amendment rights. U.S. District Judge Loren AliKhan granted ABC's request for a temporary restraining order and a preliminary injunction after the network accused the FCC of violating its right to free speech in retaliation against programming that the federal government did not support. "This is not a close case," AliKhan wrote in her ruling, saying the network was likely to succeed on First Amendment grounds. ABC proved "a campaign of retaliation against them in response to their exercise of their First Amendment rights," the judge said, noting that this showed an "irreparable injury." ABC MORE CAUTIOUS OF BOOKING CANDIDATES ON 'THE VIEW' AMID FCC PRESSURE, DISNEY'S FIRST AMENDMENT LAWSUIT SAYS ABC praised the judge's decision, calling it "an important victory for the First Amendment." The network had also asked the judge to temporarily bar the FCC from taking "any actions, formal or informal," meant to pressure or threaten penalties aimed at influencing its "exercise of editorial discretion." But the judge rejected that request, noting that the network had not specified what those future threats could entail outside the early license renewal proceedings. The FCC, meanwhile, claimed the portion of the ruling that granted ABC's motion "is wrong on the facts and wrong on the law." ABC ACCUSES FCC OF TRYING TO 'INFLICT MAXIMAL COERCIVE PRESSURE' WITH PROBE AGAINST NETWORK "While we appreciate the district court denying in part Disney's request for preliminary injunctive relief, the portion of the decision granting Disney's motion is wrong on the facts and wrong on the law — as controlling Supreme Court precedent makes clear," the agency said in a statement. "The FCC looks forward to prevailing in full on this matter. We will continue to use our lawful authority to hold broadcasters accountable to their public interest obligations." Wednesday's decision comes after ABC and Disney sued the FCC and its commissioner, Brendan Carr, in August following the commission's unusual move to order eight ABC-owned stations to submit renewal applications for their broadcast licenses years before they were set to expire. Carr, a staunch ally of President Donald Trump, ordered the early review of the stations’ licenses in April in response to a joke made by ABC's late-night host Jimmy Kimmel. Just days later, a gunman attempted to rush into the actual WHCA Dinner in Washington, D. C. The joke angered Trump and the first lady, prompting the president to demand Kimmel be fired. articles.title: Rani Kapur reportedly asks for Rs 6,000 crore to settle Karisma Kapoor's former husband Sunjay Kapur estate row, SC calls off mediation
articles.summary: Sunjay Kapur's estate is at the centre of an ongoing legal battle.
articles.body: Sunjay Kapur's estate is at the centre of an ongoing legal battle. The late businessman, Karisma Kapoor's former husband, has an alleged will that reportedly leaves everything to his wife, Priya Sachdev Kapur. Karisma's children, Samaira and Kiaan, have challenged the document as forged, and his mother, Rani Kapur, has also questioned its authenticity. In April this year, the Delhi High Court directed Priya to preserve his assets until the matter is decided, and the Supreme Court later referred the family dispute to mediation. Now, a fresh development has emerged in the case.Rani Kapur's Rs 6,000 crore settlement demandAs per a Bar and Bench report, his mother, Rani Kapur, is said to have asked for Rs 6,000 crore in return for a settlement. In the meantime, the Supreme Court has called off the mediation process.Rani Kapur calls Sunjay Kapur estate dispute 'deeply painful'Earlier, Rani Kapur had called the ongoing dispute over the will and family trust "deeply painful" and "personal," saying it was ultimately about safeguarding her family's legacy. Speaking to ANI, she said the matter went beyond legalities. "It’s very hurtful for me because my husband made this trust and gave everything to me," she said, referring to the RK family trust. She added that the business and properties were built over several decades by her late husband, and that she herself had helped build the company and their family home after moving from Mumbai to Delhi.Rani Kapur's allegations against Priya KapurRani alleged that things began to change after Sunjay's marriage to Priya Kapur. According to her, Priya started taking charge of the business soon after Sunjay's death. Rani said she finds it hard to accept claims over a legacy that was built long before Priya joined the family.Rani Kapur's notice to Priya Kapur over trustee roleFor those who may not know, Rani had issued Priya a formal notice asking her to cease acting as a trustee. She said Priya's removal became effective once the notice period was over, and argued that any effort to challenge her position in the trust was "legally invalid." Reflecting on her relationship with Sunjay, Rani made further personal allegations. "She wouldn’t have had the guts to have a dispute if Sunjay had been alive," she said. She also claimed that she and her son shared a close bond, and that he seldom made major decisions without involving her. articles.title: Aitana incendia Instagram: su colaboración internacional más esperada con un artista de más de 20 millones de oyentes mensuales está cada vez más cerca
articles.standfirst: Un adelanto y un recuerdo de 2018 añaden expectación al próximo lanzamiento
articles.summary: Un adelanto y un recuerdo de 2018 añaden expectación al próximo lanzamiento
articles.body: Aitana ha dado una pista sobre una de sus colaboraciones más esperadas. La cantante aparece en primer plano en un vídeo, mientras su acompañante toca una guitarra al fondo. La publicación apunta a un adelanto del tema que preparan juntos. La escena prescinde del despliegue de una escenario de música: una guitarra, un taburete y Aitana frente a la cámara protagonizan el fragmento. El contenido permite acercarse a la propuesta, aunque la imagen compartida no incluye una fecha de lanzamiento ni permite confirmar cuándo estará disponible la canción completa. Su compañero es Martin Garrix, el productor que supera los 20 millones de oyentes mensuales en Spotify. El audio aparece identificado como ‘Not Giving Up On Us’ y atribuido a ambos artistas, reforzando la conexión entre la publicación y una colaboración que ya había comenzado a sonar en sus conciertos. En octubre, Garrix presentó el tema durante su paso por Ciudad de México, donde se pudo escuchar a Aitana alternando español e inglés. Aquel adelanto confirmó una unión sobre la que llevaban tiempo circulando rumores. Posteriormente, LOS40 recogió que el productor situaba esta canción como próximo adelanto de ‘MARTY’, su álbum anunciado para el 5 de marzo de 2027. Aitana reaccionó entonces con entusiasmo: “Todavía no me lo creo. Me muero”. El nuevo vídeo añade otra pieza a esa promoción previa al estreno. Otro vídeo compartido por el DJ añade una anécdota. Aitana le muestra una grabación del 23 de agosto de 2018: estaba haciendo cola para entrar a su actuación cuando sonaba su canción favorita. Ambos revisan el recuerdo entre risas. “Siento que te perdieras tu canción favorita”, bromea Garrix en el texto de la publicación. “Espero que Not Giving Up On Us sea tu nueva favorita”, añade, convirtiendo aquel recuerdo como admiradora en un guiño a su trabajo conjunto.

articles.title: Ravi Kishan recalls father beating him with leather belt for pursuing acting: ‘He wanted to kill me’
articles.summary: Ask Gen Z about Ravi Kishan, and you might hear about his viral reels, and punchy one-liners.
articles.body: Ask Gen Z about Ravi Kishan, and you might hear about his viral reels, and punchy one-liners.The actor, who has worked extensively across Hindi and regional cinema, has become a popular face on social media. However, his journey to the film industry was anything but smooth.In a recent revelation, Kishan opened up about the difficult experiences he went through when his family refused to accept his decision to pursue acting.During a recent appearance on Koffee With Karan, Ravi opened up about the difficult beginning of his acting journey and recalled how his father strongly opposed his decision to enter the entertainment industry.Recalling his childhood, the actor shared that his father, who ran a milk business, wanted him to either join the family business or secure a government job. However, things took a difficult turn when Ravi performed in a Ramleela and wore a saree for his role. His father was furious when he saw him dressed that way and beat him with a leather belt. Recalling the incident, Ravi said, “He beat me very badly with a leather belt.” He also remembered his father’s question, “You want to become a nachaniya (female dancer)?”The ‘Tere Naam’ actor also shared that his father was so furious that he wanted to “kill” him. “My mother then helped me escape from there because my father wanted to kill me, believing that I had brought shame to the family,” he said. View this post on InstagramA post shared by Karan Johar (@karanjohar)Ravi eventually went on to build a career that took him across several film industries. He began acting in Hindi cinema in the early 1990s before becoming one of the recognised faces of Bhojpuri films. He also worked in Telugu and other regional-language projects.Over the years, he appeared in films such as ‘Tere Naam,’ ‘Mukkabaaz,’ ‘Sye Raa Narasimha Reddy’ and ‘Batla House.’ His performance as MLA Chhote in Kiran Rao’s ‘Laapataa Ladies’ (2024) brought him renewed attention, with audiences appreciating his portrayal in the film.In recent years, Ravi has also found a younger audience through viral clips and memes featuring his expressions and dialogues. His popularity on social media among Gen Z has introduced his work to viewers who may not have followed his career from its early days.Alongside acting, Ravi has been serving as the Member of Parliament from Gorakhpur since 2019. His recent projects include Son of Sardaar 2 and Daaku Maharaaj (2025), as well as Mirzapur: The Movie (2026).Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Bhumi Pednekar pays tribute to 26/11 martyrs at Gateway of India, calls Mumbai attacks an assault on India's sovereignty
articles.summary: Actor Bhumi Pednekar paid tribute to police officers and personnel who lost their lives in the 26/11Mumbai terrorattacks at the Gateway of India on its
articles.body: Actor Bhumi Pednekar paid tribute to police officers and personnel who lost their lives in the 26/11Mumbai terrorattacks at the Gateway of India on its 18th anniversary on Thursday.The actress, along with several other leaders, attended the memorial event marking the anniversary of the 2008Mumbai terrorattacks, in which several people, including security personnel, lost their lives.Pednekar paid tribute to the security personnel by honouring them with floral garlands as a mark of respect and gratitude for their courage, dedication and sacrifices in safeguarding the nation during the terror attack in Mumbai.After paying the tribute, the actor described the 26/11 Mumbai attacks as an assault on "India's sovereignty", highlighting the importance of remembering the sacrifices of police personnel, armed forces, first responders and victims.While talking to ANI, she said, "On 26/11, what happened wasn't just an attack on our city. It was an attack on the sovereignty of all of India. Platforms like this are so important because we need to be reminded of the sacrifice of our police officers, our first responders, those who lost their lives, and their families. India is never going to stand for hatred and terrorism. It will always remind us of the sacrifices made by our police officers and armed forces, and of the way the city keeps coming back time and again."This year marks 18 years since terrorists from the Pakistan-backed Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) unleashed mayhem on the streets of India's financial capital, Mumbai. articles.summary: Documentary film 'Amit Atal' - based on the remarkable personality and contributions of Bharat Ratna and former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee - was
articles.body: Documentary film 'Amit Atal' - based on the remarkable personality and contributions of Bharat Ratna and former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee - was screened at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa.The film has been directed by Hitesh Shankar, Editor of Panchjanya. Notably, Vajpayee was also the founding editor of Panchjanya.The documentary is highly relevant and emotionally moving, bringing alive several historical events and lesser-known anecdotes associated with Atal Ji. Through his writings, poetry and powerful speeches, Atal Ji left an indelible impression not only in India but also across the world. Amit Atal authentically portrays the lesser-known aspects of his extraordinary journey—from being a swayamsevak and pracharak to becoming an inspiring poet, distinguished journalist, visionary editor and ultimately the Prime Minister of India.Earlier, Goa Chief Minister Pramod Sawant also tweeted about the film, writing, "The film authentically portrays previously untold aspects of Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee’s journey from a volunteer to Prime Minister."गोवा में आज गूंजेगी अटल गाथा! articles.title: 'Dr Hassan' trailer out: Nawazuddin Siddiqui plays a rude but brilliant doctor in Rohan Sippy's Indian version of 'House'; jokes, 'They think nepo kids have no brains'
articles.summary: The trailer of 'Dr Hassan', the Indian adaptation of the American medical drama 'House', is finally here.
articles.body: The trailer of 'Dr Hassan', the Indian adaptation of the American medical drama 'House', is finally here. Nawazuddin Siddiqui steps into the shoes originally worn by Hugh Laurie, playing a sharp-minded but tactless doctor who cracks baffling cases. The series arrives on JioHotstar on December 11.A genius doctor with no filterThe trailer begins inside Janki Das Ruia Hospital, where certain illnesses refuse to reveal their cause. The one person who can often solve them is Dr Hassan, a doctor who spots clues that everyone else misses. His brain is built for complicated diagnoses, but ordinary human interaction is a different story. He speaks bluntly to patients and colleagues alike, which makes him hard to work with, yet his talent ensures the hospital cannot do without him.The team around HassanDia Mirza appears as Dr Palak Jain, the hospital's Chief Medical Officer. She studied medicine with Hassan and knows his abilities better than most. Dr Vivek is his closest friend and confidant, while Smaran Sahu, Rehmat Rattan and Jayson Thaam play specialist doctors who must adjust to a boss who seldom plays by the book. Together, they handle the toughest and most puzzling medical cases.Nawazuddin Siddiqui's nepo kids jibeThe trailer also shows Nawazuddin Siddiqui's sense of humour. In one scene, a colleague helps crack part of a case, and Hassan applauds him with a dose of sarcasm. He says, "Very good, Rishi, take the charge. They think nepo kids have no brains."About 'Dr Hassan' and 'House'Sippy directs the series, which has been adapted and scripted by Vinay Chhawal and Ketan Pedgaonkar, with dialogues by Virat Basoya. Banijay Asia backs the project, with Deepak Dhar, Rishi Negi, Rajesh Chadha, Mrinalini Jain and Shyam Rathi as producers and Vibhas Singh Gautam as Executive Producer.'Dr Hassan' is based on 'House', created by David Shore. The original, led by Hugh Laurie, ran for eight seasons on FOX between 2004 and 2012. It collected five Primetime Emmy Awards, two Golden Globe Awards, a Peabody Award and nine People's Choice Awards, among other honours. Besides Nawazuddin and Dia, the Indian version features Smaran Sahu, Rehmat Rattan and Jayson Thaam in key roles.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Visions of Modernity brings Dalí, Picasso and Chagall together
articles.summary: Salvador Dalí, Pablo Picasso, and Marc Chagall worked in the same era but saw the world in very different ways.
articles.body: Salvador Dalí, Pablo Picasso, and Marc Chagall worked in the same era but saw the world in very different ways. Dalí explored dreams and the subconscious through Surrealism, Picasso broke with conventional representation as a pioneer of Cubism, and Chagall drew on childhood memories, faith, and cultural traditions to create dreamlike compositions. Visions of Modernity, presented by Studio Verasa, places their work side by side in what is billed as the first exhibition of its kind in India.Twenty-Four Works, Three MastersThe show features 24 graphic works: 11 by Dalí, 7 by Picasso, and 6 by Chagall. Three bronze sculptures by Dalí are also on display. The selection includes etchings, lithographs, and hand-signed editions.Dalí's contributions come from series such as Holy Grail, Francisco Goya's Los Caprichos, Les Songes Drolatiques de Pantagruel, and Flor Dalí. His sculptures include the iconic Homage to Newton, Lady Godiva, and Triumphant Elephant. Picasso's works include lithographs from the Marina Picasso Collection, hand-signed and authenticated by Marina Picasso, along with a graphic associated with the Suite Vollard. Chagall's selection includes graphics from a series he created in collaboration with the poet Louis Aragon.Built on a Collector's VisionThe works draw on Dalí Universe, an international collection of Dalí's art assembled over more than 50 years by Italian collector and entrepreneur Beniamino Levi. Through his Milan gallery, Galleria Levi, Levi built relationships with major artists including Picasso, Miró, Chagall, and Magritte. Studio Verasa is the exclusive representative and exhibitor of Dalí Universe in India.Founder and curator Aarohi Garg first came to art during four years in Spain, where she spent afternoons in museums with Dalí, Sorolla, Miró, and Velázquez. She later studied at Sotheby's in London and founded Studio Verasa at 23 to bring significant international art to Indian audiences. Her curatorial approach focuses on the artists' lives, the people they knew, and the places that shaped their work. The exhibition, she hopes, will encourage visitors, from seasoned collectors to first-time gallery goers, to look a little closer and discover the stories beyond the canvas.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
